key.name: pinned
key.summary: What's pinned to the taskbar, in order
key.description: Each entry is an app's desktop file ID ("org.gnome.TextEditor.desktop") or a role: "role:web", "role:terminal", "role:files", "role:mail", "role:documents", "role:spreadsheets", "role:presentations", "role:pdf" or "role:art". A role is a slot for whichever app is the default for that job: it opens that app, and the app's windows show under it. A role no installed app does isn't shown.

key.name: size
key.summary: The taskbar's size
key.description: Small (32 pixels), medium (42) or large (52), with its icons to match. Patrone Settings sets it.

key.name: layout
key.summary: Where the taskbar and its buttons go
key.description: "left": along the bottom, the menu button and the apps on the left. "center": the menu button and the apps in the middle. "split": the menu button on the left, the apps in the middle. "top": along the top of the screen, the menu button and the apps on the left, menus opening downward. The theme doesn't change it. Patrone Settings sets it.

key.name: start-icon
key.summary: The menu button's icon
key.description: "patrone" is the Patrone P in its colors, "orb" a blue orb with a white P. The others take the taskbar's text color: "mono" (the P), "grid" (a grid of dots), "menu" (three lines), "circle", "spark" (a four-pointed star) and "terminal" (a prompt). Patrone Settings sets it.

key.name: color
key.summary: Where the taskbar's color comes from
key.description: "wallpaper": the wallpaper's own hue, dark or light with the style, in the Patrone, Modern and Studio themes. "theme": the theme's own grey. Classic and Sapphire ("royal") always keep their own colors. Patrone Settings sets it.

key.name: pin-icons
key.summary: The icons of the web, terminal, files and mail pins
key.description: "patrone": Patrone's own icons for each job (a globe, a prompt, a folder, an envelope), whichever app does it. "app": the icon of the app each one opens. Patrone Settings sets it.

key.name: show-recycle-bin
key.summary: Show the Recycle Bin on the desktop
key.description: Patrone's own, in place of the desktop icons extension's trash.

key.name: recycle-bin-dock
key.summary: The corner the Recycle Bin stays docked to
key.description: A corner of the primary screen, inside the taskbar, or "none" to leave it wherever it's dragged (recycle-bin-position). Its right-click menu sets it; dragged while docked, it docks to the nearest corner.

key.name: recycle-bin-position
key.summary: Where the Recycle Bin is when it isn't docked
key.description: Across and down the screen's free area, each from 0 to 1, so it stays in place when the screen size changes.

key.name: desktop-files
key.summary: Where the desktop's files show
key.description: "desktop", the default: Patrone File Manager shows the files in the Desktop folder on the desktop. "panel": a small pill at the left edge of the primary screen, shown while no window covers it, opens them in a panel that slides out over the windows as a full layer of the screen, and closes when a window opens. "hidden": a clean desktop, with nothing on it, not even the Recycle Bin (whatever show-recycle-bin says); the same panel opens from the desktop-files-corner, or the desktop's or the taskbar's right-click menu. Patrone Settings sets it, on its Desktop page.

key.name: desktop-files-corner
key.summary: The corner that shows the desktop's files on a clean desktop
key.description: Pointing at this corner of the primary screen shows the files, and pointing at it again hides them. It does nothing while something else uses the corner (desktop-corners-in-use).

key.name: desktop-corners-in-use
key.summary: Which screen corners something else uses, and what
key.description: The taskbar keeps this up to date, for the Settings apps, which offer only the other corners for desktop-files-corner. Each is "corner:user", where the user is taskbar, window-buttons, hot-corner or screen. Not for setting by hand.

key.name: desktop-bubble
key.summary: Replaced by desktop-files
key.description: The yes-or-no this was until 2026-10-30. Read once, so an account that set it keeps its choice in desktop-files.

key.name: desktop-bubble-introduced
key.summary: Whether the panel's pill has been opened yet
key.description: Until it has, its pill bounces now and then, with a tip saying what it does.

key.name: ding-replaced
key.summary: Whether the taskbar turned Ubuntu's desktop icons off
key.description: Patrone File Manager draws the desktop in place of Ubuntu's desktop icons extension, so the taskbar adds that extension to GNOME's disabled-extensions while it does. This remembers that it did, so it can turn the extension back on if File Manager's desktop goes (not installed, or failing to start).

key.name: terminal-app
key.summary: The app the terminal slot opens
key.description: A desktop file ID. Empty: Patrone Terminal, or another terminal if it isn't installed. (The other slots but art follow the system's default apps instead.)

key.name: art-app
key.summary: The app the art slot opens
key.description: A desktop file ID. Empty: ArtCraft, else LibreOffice Draw, GIMP, Krita, Inkscape or Pinta, whichever is installed first, else another drawing app. (Drawing has no file type of its own to take the default app of.)

key.name: web-search-url
key.summary: Where web searches from the Patrone menu go
key.description: "%s" is replaced with the search terms. Opened with the default web browser.

key.name: sign-in-terminal
key.summary: Whether the terminal opens at sign-in, and where it goes
key.description: Patrone Terminal's first window after signing in. "logo": over the logo of Patrone's wallpaper, between the pictures in its corners, at any screen size (on another wallpaper, the same part of the screen). "center": at its own size, in the middle of the screen above the taskbar. It's left alone once moved, resized or maximized. "off": it doesn't open at sign-in (patrone-terminal's autostart script reads this too). Patrone Settings sets it, on its Desktop page.

key.name: suggested-apps
key.summary: Apps the Patrone menu suggests among the recent files
key.description: Desktop file IDs. Each shows in the Patrone menu's Recent (and the search button's Recent) as if it had just been opened when it was first suggested, so it starts at the top and moves down as files are opened, then drops off like any recent file. Software, Patrone's app store, by default, so people come to know it.

key.name: suggested-apps-since
key.summary: When each suggested app was first suggested
key.description: Desktop file ID to seconds since 1970. The taskbar fills it in; removing an ID suggests that app again, as new.
